notes: Machine-drafted (AI-assisted) term list; not reviewed. Needs review by a mathematician fluent in Arabic, with reviewers from both the Mashriq and the Maghreb: school terminology differs (Maghreb usage often follows French terms, e.g. 'مبرهنة' and 'تطبيق', while many Mashriq curricula use 'نظرية' and 'دالة'; Jordan and Palestine commonly use 'اقتران' for function). Terms are Modern Standard Arabic; regional attributions are indicative only and must be confirmed. Notation direction (LTR vs RTL formulas) and digit shapes are separate from terminology and are documented in docs/i18n/language-registry.md.

collection.note: School Arabic often uses the same word 'مجموعة' for an informal collection and for a set. Uncertain: the drafter could not confirm an established standard term; a fluent mathematician should supply the term actually used in teaching.

member.note: 'عنصر' is the standard term; x ∈ A is read 'x ينتمي إلى A'.

empty-set.note: 'الخالية' is common in the Mashriq; 'الفارغة' is reported in Maghreb usage. To be confirmed.

complement.note: To be confirmed; both forms are reported.

cardinality.note: 'عدد العناصر' (number of elements) is the school phrase. University-level term: Uncertain: the drafter could not confirm an established standard term; a fluent mathematician should supply the term actually used in teaching.

integer.note: Maghreb curricula, following French 'entier relatif', often use 'عدد صحيح نسبي' for elements of ℤ and 'عدد صحيح طبيعي' for elements of ℕ.

natural-number.note: Whether 0 is included varies; Maghreb curricula following the French convention include 0.

additive-inverse.note: 'مقابل' (opposite) is reported in Maghreb usage. To be confirmed.

function.note: 'اقتران' is used in Jordan and Palestine; 'تطبيق' (map, from French 'application') is common in the Maghreb for maps between sets.

domain.note: 'مجموعة التعريف' (domain of definition) and 'مجموعة الانطلاق' (departure set) are reported in Maghreb usage. To be confirmed.

codomain.note: 'مجموعة الوصول' (arrival set, from French 'ensemble d'arrivée') is reported in Maghreb usage. Uncertain: the drafter could not confirm an established standard term; a fluent mathematician should supply the term actually used in teaching.

image.note: 'المدى' (range) is often used for the image of the whole domain.

injective.note: Maghreb usage reportedly 'تطبيق تبايني' (injection: 'تباين'). Uncertain: the drafter could not confirm an established standard term; a fluent mathematician should supply the term actually used in teaching.

surjective.note: Maghreb usage reportedly 'تطبيق شمولي' (surjection: 'شمول'). Uncertain: the drafter could not confirm an established standard term; a fluent mathematician should supply the term actually used in teaching.

bijective.note: Maghreb usage reportedly 'تطبيق تقابلي' (bijection: 'تقابل'). To be confirmed.

identity-function.note: Uncertain: the drafter could not confirm an established standard term; a fluent mathematician should supply the term actually used in teaching.

theorem.note: 'مبرهنة' is usual in the Maghreb and in much university usage; 'نظرية' is common in many Mashriq school curricula (it also means 'theory').

modular-arithmetic.note: 'الموافقة بترديد n' (congruence modulo n) is reported in Maghreb usage. Uncertain: the drafter could not confirm an established standard term; a fluent mathematician should supply the term actually used in teaching.

equivalence-class.note: To be confirmed which form is usual in which region.

category.note: Uncertain: the drafter could not confirm an established standard term; a fluent mathematician should supply the term actually used in teaching.

morphism.note: 'تشاكل' usually means homomorphism, so it should not be used for an arbitrary morphism. Uncertain: the drafter could not confirm an established standard term; a fluent mathematician should supply the term actually used in teaching.

functor.note: Transliteration. Uncertain: the drafter could not confirm an established standard term; a fluent mathematician should supply the term actually used in teaching.
